newsitem.title: NORWAY: Esso mulls new Norway production ship - report.
newsitem.headline: Esso mulls new Norway production ship - report.

text.p: Esso Norge is considering building a production ship to develop new oil discoveries near to the Balder field in the North Sea, the daily Stavanger Aftenblad said on Thursday.
In April the Norwegian Oil Directorate (OD) confirmed that Esso and Enterprise Oil had discovered oil and gas in block 25/10, 15 km southwest of Balder. The find was tentatively-dubbed Hanz.
Earlier this month the OD announced Esso alone had found oil in block 25/8 north of Balder. That find was called Forseti, Stavanger Aftenblad said.
The newspaper said geologists were working to come up with estimates of the size of the finds, while Esso was considering different development solutions.

"Which solution we decide upon is dependent on what the geologists find," the daily quoted Hugo Skandsen, Esso head spokesman, as saying. "If it happens that we find more oil in the area, we could be looking at a new production ship."
"However, the most likely scenario at the moment is to tie Hanz and Forseti back to the existing Balder installation and phase in the oil as output at the Balder field decreases," Skandsen said.

Esso's 4.7 billion crown Balder project is being developed using subsea wells tied into a floating production vessel. It is the first dedicated installation of this type on the Norwegian continental shelf.

On Wednesday Esso confirmed it had delayed the start up of Balder for a second time. It said it did not see September as a likely date for the field to come on stream, but it could not give a new timetable for operations to begin.

Balder, with recoverable reserves estimated at 170 million barrels, is expected to add 75,000 barrels per day to Norwegian production at peak output. It was originally scheduled to start up between the end of 1996 and the beginning of the second quarter 1997.
